source.title: Confidence drives a neural confirmation bias

confidence_rationale: Highest mapping fidelity of any entry in this directory: the asymmetry is driven BY a confidence/precision variable and acts ON subsequent evidence integration, which is structurally the self-reinforcing precision loop SD-076 encodes. MEG plus computational modelling, strong venue. Held below 0.85 because it is a within-trial post-decisional effect on perceptual evidence, not a slow across-episode drift in a variance estimate.
failure_signatures: Disconfirmatory evidence processing was ABOLISHED rather than merely attenuated at high confidence -- a linear two-rate EMA cannot produce a hard gate, so SD-076's functional form may understate the effect at the high-precision end where runaway inflation is most dangerous.

The effect is driven by confidence in a JUST-MADE choice; if REE's rv update is not conditioned on the agent's own commitment, the analogous gating has no trigger and SD-076 reduces to an unmotivated constant asymmetry.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Holding high confidence in a decision modulates post-decisional neural processing so that integration of confirmatory evidence is amplified while integration of disconfirmatory evidence is abolished, producing a selective neural gating for choice-consistent information.
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads this as evidence that the asymmetry SD-076 posits is not a fixed constant but is GATED BY the very precision estimate it inflates -- high confidence suppresses the disconfirming evidence that would correct it. That closes SD-076 into a positive-feedback loop, which is the strongest available argument that waking precision drift is self-amplifying and therefore requires a periodic external corrective of the kind MECH-204 supplies.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a WITHIN-TRIAL post-decisional effect on perceptual evidence accumulation over hundreds of milliseconds, whereas SD-076 is an ACROSS-EPISODE drift in a running variance estimate. The timescales differ by orders of magnitude and the paper offers no evidence that the within-trial gating accumulates into a slow bias. Treating the two as the same mechanism at different rates is an assumption REE is making, not a finding.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans, MEG, two-stage perceptual discrimination task with post-decisional evidence and confidence report.

confidence_components.notes: Mapping fidelity weighted heavily here because SD-076 is a design_decision about a precision variable and this is the one retrieved paper where the manipulated and measured quantity IS confidence/precision rather than world-belief. Transfer risk is the timescale gap, not the species or modality.
